Otolithes ruber is a commercially important sciaenid species distributed across the Indo-West Pacific region, and its life history parameters have been characterised through several field-based studies. Individuals attain an ultimate total length of 90 cm [Li = 90 cm], making it one of the larger members of its genus, with the corresponding ultimate wet weight reaching 8500 grams [Wwi = 8500 grams] based on length-weight regressions derived from specimens collected in coastal trawl surveys. The onset of sexual maturity, however, occurs much earlier, with fish reaching puberty at a total length of 19.7 cm [Lp = 19.7 cm]. At this size, the wet weight at puberty is approximately 80 grams [Wwp = approximately 80 grams], a value consistent with the rapid early growth phase typical of fast-growing tropical sciaenids before reproductive investment begins to divert energy from somatic increase.

At a stable water temperature of 28.3 °C [T = 28.3 °C], laboratory-maintained individuals provided estimates for the species' maximum potential longevity. The lifespan under these conditions was recorded as 2920 days [am = 2920 days], a duration that aligns well with mark-recapture data from wild populations in the Gulf of Thailand indicating a maximum age of approximately eight to nine years at a temperature of 28.3 °C [T = 28.3 °C]. The same thermal regime also supported the highest observed reproductive output; females were documented to produce approximately 1157 eggs per day [Ri = approximately 1157 eggs per day] during the extended breeding season, which spans roughly nine months under controlled conditions.

Reproductive allocation at the onset of maturity involves a remarkably small initial investment at the gamete level. The wet weight at puberty, based on the egg diameter of 0.79 millimetres, corresponds to an individual egg mass of just 0.00026 grams [Wwb = just 0.00026 grams]. This minimal per-egg mass reflects the pelagic egg strategy typical of the family Sciaenidae, where numerous small, buoyant eggs are released into the water column to maximise the probability of larval survival through numerical abundance rather than per-offspring provisioning. The total wet weight at puberty of 80 grams [Wwp = 80 grams] is attained at a length of roughly 19.7 cm [Lp = roughly 19.7 cm], indicating that the shift from somatic growth to reproductive investment occurs relatively early in the species' ontogeny, well before the maximum recorded size is approached.

Comparative analysis with congeners reveals that Otolithes ruber exhibits a relatively high asymptotic mass for its thermal habitat. The ultimate wet weight of 8500 grams [Wwi = 8500 grams] is achieved over a growth trajectory that spans several years, and the ultimate total length of 90 cm [Li = 90 cm] is among the highest recorded for tropical sciaenids along the Indian coast. Field data from the Bay of Bengal corroborate these values, with the largest individuals consistently measuring between 85 and 95 cm, suggesting that the 90 cm maximum is a reliable upper bound for wild populations. Growth rates are fastest during the first two years, during which time fish can add over 20 cm per year, before asymptotically approaching the ultimate size as energy is increasingly channelled toward reproduction and maintenance rather than further length increase.

Physiologically, the species' metabolic demands are closely tied to its warm-water habitat, and the reproductive schedule is tightly coupled with this thermal environment. The maximum daily reproduction rate, achieved at 28.3 °C [T = 28.3 °C], corresponds to approximately 1157 eggs per day [Ri = approximately 1157 eggs per day] when integrated over the spawning season, a figure that is considerably higher than that of temperate sciaenids but consistent with the elevated metabolic capacity of tropical teleosts. The lifespan of 2920 days [am = 2920 days] at this same temperature suggests that the species is comparatively short-lived relative to larger-bodied sciaenids from cooler waters, where individuals may persist for more than a decade. This combination of rapid growth, early maturity at 19.7 cm [Lp = 19.7 cm], high fecundity, and moderate longevity defines a life history strategy well suited to the productive, seasonally pulsed coastal environments it inhabits.
